title: BFCM fulfillment checklist: 6 things to finalize before Black Friday
summary: Prepare for Black Friday and Cyber Monday with a practical BFCM fulfillment checklist covering inventory, warehouse capacity, shipping and more.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


- **Verify inventory availability:** Confirm BFCM inventory is received, processed, and ready to fulfill, and identify potential stockout risks.
- **Check fulfillment capacity:** Confirm your 3PL can accommodate forecasted demand and understand any volume-related SLA limitations.
- **Align marketing and operations:** Verify that fulfillment plans reflect the latest promotional schedules and demand forecasts.
- **Review order and shipping workflows:** Check order routing, shipping rules, and delivery expectations before volume spikes.
- **Prepare for disruptions:** Establish clear responses to stockouts, order backlogs, and shipping delays.
- **Monitor performance:** Track inventory levels, aging orders, and fulfillment exceptions throughout BFCM.


Black Friday and Cyber Monday (BFCM) are almost here. Your promotions are planned, inventory has been ordered, and demand forecasts are in place. But is your fulfillment operation ready for the rush?


With Black Friday approaching, and Cyber Monday to quickly follow, now is the time to catch potential issues before order volumes spike.


This BFCM fulfillment checklist walks through six essential checks to help ecommerce brands prepare for increased demand, avoid disruptions, and keep orders moving throughout the busiest shopping weekend of the year.


## 1. Confirm inventory is ready to fulfill


Inventory may be in transit, awaiting receiving, or reserved for specific sales channels. Before BFCM, verify how much stock is available to fulfill orders, especially for products featured in upcoming promotions.


Compare available inventory against demand forecasts to identify potential shortages. For brands selling across multiple channels, review inventory allocations to ensure a surge in DTC demand doesn't affect stock reserved for marketplaces or retail partners.


**Your inventory checklist:**


- Confirm BFCM inventory has been received, processed, and made available for fulfillment; flag any outstanding shipments
- Verify available-to-sell inventory for your highest-demand SKUs
- Compare inventory levels against projected BFCM demand
- Review inventory allocations across DTC, marketplaces, and retail channels
- Identify stockout risks and adjust promotions or replenishment plans accordingly


For brands managing[omnichannel fulfillment across B2B and retail](https://flow.space/blog/omnichannel-fulfillment-b2b-retail) , inventory allocation is especially important during BFCM. A surge in DTC orders can quickly deplete stock reserved for retail partners or wholesale commitments. Review channel-specific allocations before promotions begin to protect inventory availability and avoid disruptions across sales channels.


## 2. Verify warehouse capacity and fulfillment timelines


Your fulfillment operation might comfortably handle an average day's orders. BFCM and[peak season fulfillment](https://flow.space/blog/peak-season-fulfillment-checklist) is a different test.


A successful promotion can generate several days' worth of demand in just a few hours. Your fulfillment provider needs to understand not only how many orders you expect, but when they're likely to arrive.


Confirm that staffing, warehouse schedules, and processing capacity align with your forecast.


**Your fulfillment capacity checklist:**


- Share expected order volumes, including anticipated spikes during major promotions
- Confirm warehouse staffing and operating schedules throughout BFCM
- Review order-processing cutoffs and fulfillment timelines
- Verify that promotional bundles or special packaging requirements are supported
- Establish a point of contact for urgent fulfillment issues


Ask your fulfillment partner what happens if orders exceed your forecast. Volume limits may affect fulfillment SLAs, **meaning orders above an agreed threshold could face longer processing times.**


During BFCM, an unexpected surge in demand can quickly put additional pressure on warehouse operations. Confirm how much additional volume your provider can accommodate, whether processing timelines change, and how unexpected spikes will be handled.


## 3. Confirm marketing and fulfillment plans are aligned


Last-minute campaign changes can affect fulfillment demand, even when teams have spent months preparing for BFCM.


An increase in advertising spend, an extended flash sale, or overlapping promotions could push order volumes beyond the original forecast. Review your final campaign calendar with your operations team and fulfillment provider to catch any changes that may affect inventory availability or processing capacity.


**Your marketing and operations checklist:**


- Confirm your fulfillment provider has the latest promotional calendar and demand forecasts
- Flag changes to featured SKUs, bundles, or expected order volumes
- Verify promotional offers align with available inventory
- Review overlapping campaigns that could create unexpected order spikes
- Establish how last-minute campaign changes will be communicated and approved


Don't forget to account for promotions that overlap. An email campaign, paid social promotion, and marketplace sale running simultaneously can create a larger spike than any individual campaign suggests.


## 4. Double-check order routing and shipping workflows


The last thing you want during BFCM is discovering that orders aren't flowing correctly from your storefront to your fulfillment provider.


Review your integrations and shipping configurations before traffic increases. Pay particular attention to changes introduced for holiday promotions, such as new product bundles, shipping offers, or marketplace listings.


**Your order and shipping checklist:**


- Verify that orders are flowing correctly from each active sales channel
- Test any new SKUs, bundles, or promotional configurations
- Review shipping methods, order cutoffs, and delivery promises
- Confirm how orders with invalid addresses, insufficient inventory, or other exceptions are handled
- Check that tracking information flows back to your sales channels


It's also worth reviewing[shipping costs during peak season](https://flow.space/blog/reduce-peak-season-fulfillment-costs) . For instance, with surcharges in effect, selecting an unnecessarily expensive shipping service can put additional pressure on margins.


Automated rate shopping can help reduce costs by selecting the lowest-cost eligible shipping option that meets each order's delivery requirements.


## 5. Prepare for fulfillment disruptions


Even well-prepared brands can encounter unexpected challenges during BFCM.


A product might sell faster than forecasted. A carrier could experience delays. An unexpected order spike might create a fulfillment backlog.


What matters is how quickly your team identifies the issue and responds.


Rather than developing a complicated contingency plan, focus on a few realistic scenarios and the decisions each one requires.


**Your contingency checklist:**


- Identify high-risk SKUs and establish a response if inventory runs low
- Agree on what happens if orders begin exceeding expected processing timelines
- Confirm who should be contacted about fulfillment or shipping disruptions
- Establish when customers should receive proactive delay notifications
- Assign owners for urgent operational decisions


For example, if a best-selling SKU runs low, your team should already know whether to pause promotions, adjust available inventory, or redirect marketing efforts toward other products.


Clear decision-making responsibilities can prevent small issues and[backorders](https://flow.space/product-releases/backorder-visibility) from becoming larger disruptions.


## 6. Decide what to monitor during BFCM


Preparation doesn't stop when Black Friday begins.


Throughout the BFCM weekend (and subsequent Cyber Week), your team needs visibility into what's happening across inventory, orders, and fulfillment operations.


Decide which metrics matter most, who will monitor them, and what should trigger action.


**Your BFCM monitoring checklist:**


- Track unfulfilled and aging orders to identify potential backlogs.
- Monitor inventory levels for high-demand products
- Review orders requiring attention, including inventory and shipping exceptions
- Establish reporting frequency and escalation procedures with your fulfillment provider


Avoid monitoring metrics without a clear purpose. Each report should help your team answer an operational question: Are orders shipping on time? Is inventory running low? Are any exceptions preventing orders from moving forward?


The sooner you spot a problem, the more options you have to address it.

## Frequently asked questions about BFCM fulfillment


### When should ecommerce brands finalize their BFCM fulfillment plans?


Ideally, major inventory, warehouse capacity, and shipping decisions should be finalized several weeks before Black Friday. In the final two to three weeks, focus on confirming inventory availability, validating order workflows, coordinating promotions, and preparing contingency plans.


### What are the biggest fulfillment risks during Black Friday and Cyber Monday?


Common risks include inventory shortages, unexpected order spikes, warehouse backlogs, shipping delays, and order-routing errors. Limited visibility across sales channels can make these problems harder to identify. Monitoring fulfillment activity and establishing clear escalation procedures can help brands respond faster.


### How can ecommerce brands avoid shipping delays during BFCM?


Start by confirming that inventory is available to fulfill, reviewing warehouse processing timelines, and checking shipping cutoffs. Make sure orders flow correctly from sales channels to your fulfillment provider, and monitor aging orders throughout the weekend. While carrier delays can't always be prevented, proactive planning and clear delivery expectations can reduce their impact.
